entries.reason: Fails criterion 1; criteria 2-5 hold. (1) NOT SHOWN TO BE A REAL MISTAKE ON THIS SHAPE. The mistakes teachers recognise on single-letter analogies are counting the start letter (lands one past, already vr14-step-size), going the wrong way (vr14-step-direction), losing your place in the alphabet, and wrapping past Z. A doubled jump is recognised in SERIES, where the child stands on the last term of a run and overshoots. That mechanism does not carry over here. The drafter's first route, 'a series habit' reading the pair and the new letter as one run, does not produce the value: read as a run, C F K has gaps of +3 and +5, so it gives no reason to take a second +3 from K. The second route, 'the first pair showed two letters and so seemed to ask for two moves', is a story built to produce the value, with no source behind it. The drafter cites no frequency, and the executor's own comment gives the motive: 'the one genuine vr-14 mistake that lands ABOVE the key; without it the key could only be second-latest.' The entry was found by looking for a value above the key and then giving it a mechanism. That is the fit the brief warns about. STEP-2 CASE: on 6 of the 18 proposed carriers (02, 06, 10, 14, 18, 22) the value is key+2. A teacher would read that as a long count, losing your place by two letters, and not as a doubled jump. On those rows the tag claims a diagnosis the value cannot carry, and the hint ('make the jump just once') then teaches against a mistake the child may not have made. Only the 12 step-3/step-4 rows put clear distance between this value and a miscount, and even there the mechanism is unproven. ALTERNATIVE: the key-rank shortcut R1030 measured has a remedy that needs no new mistake. Real letter-connection items also run BACKWARDS (D -> A, K -> ?). On a backwards row vr14-step-direction lands ABOVE the key, so a generator that mixes directions spreads the key's rank using only entries that already exist. CRITERIA THAT PASS: (2) No ACTIVE VR entry names this move for vr-14. vr-letter-series-step-repeat's hint points at 'the last letter', which an analogy does not have, and vr14-step-direction already sits beside vr-letter-series-direction door by door, so a separate entry WOULD be justified if the mistake were established. (3) The worked example is right: C(2) -> F(5) is three on; K(10) + 3 = N(13), the key on row 03; N + 3 = Q. I recomputed stemWord + 2*step on all 18 carriers and every valuesProduced entry matches. The step-1 exclusion list (01, 05, 09, 13, 17, 21, 25) is right, as are the claim that step-2..4 values sit strictly above every current option and 'highest is Z on row 20'. (4) The hint is true on every vr-14 row, describes a move, and has sentences of 7 and 10 words in plain British English. (5) The executor returns null when answer+step > 25, and the generator's steps are 1-4 with a maximum answer of 21, so nothing wraps. answer+step never equals the key, and does not match any other reading I tried (doubling the letter position on the B->D and D->H pairs, or the pair-to-stem offset, which gives the key itself). One note for the generator: at step 1 the executor still emits key+1, which is the same value as vr14-step-size, so a door listing this id first would mis-tag those rows.
